title: Multi-Agent Debate and Collaboration
service: Debate: Society-of-Minds style debates over full-mesh, star and arbitrary read topologies, with a binary transcript, a concurrent CSV-reporting runner and topology analysis; every model is a scripted fake
deviations: Part 1: the planned tie bug (final vote should go to the hub) does not exist in the lesson code, because Counter.most_common already prefers the first-inserted answer and the hub is inserted first. The tie rule is instead alphabetical, in one majority() helper used by both the debaters' drift and the final vote, so seating order never decides and the faster Counter-subtraction round gives the same answers.

Part 1: the planned over-fix guard (an answer left at count 0 after subtracting the own vote being taken as most common) cannot fail: a zero count never beats a positive one, and a debater with no peers keeps its answer. The guard checks the more common mistakes instead: the own vote never subtracted, or subtracted in place on one shared Counter.

Part 2: debater names live once in a roster header and turns refer to roster positions; a turn count up front makes a cut at a turn boundary detectable; the test pins the bytes of one small transcript so the LEB128 group order and the big-endian double are checked, not just the round trip.
Part 3: rotating a failed hub is a follow-up question, not a test; multiple hubs appear as a topology in the ops check.

Part 4: the live runner has no forced disagreement or aggregation (that is Part 3), and the CSV has one column per debater instead of one packed answers column, so quoting comes from csv itself. Concurrency is checked with an in-flight counter in the fakes, not wall time; elapsed_ms is only bounded loosely (at least 90 ms for the timeout round, under 90 ms for a 10 ms round).

Part 5: camps (mutual reachability) instead of a strongly-connected-components algorithm with a recursion-depth trap, because RecursionError traps already appear in more than two chapter-14 exams; the BFS-versus-DFS-depth trap is used instead.

parts.lesson_anchor: Sparse topology (full mesh N=5, R=3 = 60 critique ops; star = 12, spokes read only the hub); Build It: code/main.py full_mesh_round, sparse_star_round, run_debate; Convergence
planted_bugs: sparse_star_round has the hub read every spoke and counts those reads, 24 ops instead of the lesson's 12

majority() uses Counter.most_common, so a tie goes to whichever answer was seen first; the docstring wants the alphabetically first answer. It surfaces two calls up, as run_debate results that depend on seating order
run_debate keeps the first round of agreement as converged_round even after the debaters split again (copied from the lesson code)
full_mesh_round counts the other N - 1 answers separately for every debater, O(N^2)
parts.timing_assert: one full-mesh round of 5000 debaters under 0.1 s (the quadratic round takes 1.1 to 1.6 s; fixed 5 to 12 ms)
parts.overfix_guard: recording debaters check the peer votes each one receives, which rules out counting everyone once without subtracting the own vote, or subtracting it in place on a shared Counter. Two checks also stop half fixes: the same recorders on a star check that the hub receives nothing, so dropping only the hub's op count fails; three debaters holding one answer each tie 1-1 inside every drift, in both seatings, so fixing the tie only in run_debate's final vote fails

parts.lesson_anchor: Society of Minds: N proposers, R rounds, each debater reading its peers; Exercise 2 (debaters return answer and confidence)
parts.storage: binary format fixed by the module docstring: MAGIC, unsigned LEB128 varints for counts, rounds and roster positions, UTF-8 text with a byte-length prefix, big-endian IEEE 754 doubles
parts.exactness: a 20000-debater roster and turns with confidences 0.1 + 0.2, 1/3, 5e-324 and -0.0 (checked with struct.pack), answers with non-ASCII, CJK, an emoji, NUL and an empty string, round 300, debater 19999 and peers 16384, 0, 127, 128 in reading order round-trip through a file and write the same bytes again; one small transcript matches exact bytes
